text:
ryan.cust: Hey team — seen a sudden spike of 503s hitting our integration. Happens when we regen responses in parallel while also firing embeds. Not rate limited 429s, straight 503 Service Unavailable. Example request id: req_8b3a2f, time ~2026-03-17T14:12:03Z. We're on rwd-32k-v2, ~11–14k tokens per request, concurrency ~12, roughly 1.8k RPM total across the app. Any quick checks?

alex.support: Thanks Ryan — can you confirm: are these streaming responses or non-streaming? Also are the embed requests to Redwood API or an internal embed pipeline? 503s likely indicate overloaded serving instances rather than auth.

ryan.cust: Non-streaming generation. Embeds go to the same Redwood hosted embeddings endpoint (separate call). We typically do 6 parallel regen requests + ~8 parallel embed calls on user save.

maria.eng: that pattern (regen + parallel embed fanout) is a classic slot-starvation case for the 32k model. Two quick things to check: 1) do you see X-RateLimit-* headers (X-RateLimit-RPM, X-RateLimit-Token-TPM) in responses? 2) capture a sample req_id and the full response body for a 503 — sometimes runtime returns a short diagnostic like "slot_allocation_failed" or "instance_overloaded".

ryan.cust: I grabbed another id: req_9f7d1a. Response body was just 503, no JSON. No X-RateLimit headers present.

maria.eng: Ok. Lack of X-RateLimit headers suggests requests were routed to runtime that couldn't accept the work (internal queue overflow) rather than a clean quota rejection. For 32k variants we have lower concurrent slot counts per instance and token-based throughput caps. If you send heavy token requests concurrently + embed fanout, you can exhaust instance capacity and trigger immediate 503s.

alex.support: Can you also share whether you're using hosted multi-model fanout (parallel calls to different variants) or a single model? And do you pin a model version?

ryan.cust: Single model, pinned to rwd-32k-v2. No multi-model fanout.

jen.ops: Jumping in — from infra side I see a short window at 14:12:02–14:12:06 where several nodes serving rwd-32k-v2 hit high GPU mem pressure and started returning 503s while shedding new requests. Internal log snippet for that window: `ERROR allocation.cpp: slot_allocation_failed: no free slots for model rwd-32k-v2` — looks like concurrent slot exhaustion.

maria.eng: Recommended mitigations: 1) reduce client concurrency (try cap at 4 concurrent gen requests while embeds are running). 2) serialize or batch embeddings where possible (embedding calls are cheap but fanout matters). 3) implement jittered exponential backoff on 5xx and avoid aggressive immediate retries. 4) optionally route embeddings to a different API key or dedicated pool if you have Dedicated capacity.

alex.support: Repro steps we ask customers to try so we can triage quickly: 
1) Reproduce with a single user: set concurrency to 4 (regen) and sequentialize embeddings. 
2) If 503s disappear, gradually raise parallelism and note the threshold. 
3) Collect two request_ids (one 200 and one 503) and paste them here. 
4) Capture a curl with verbose headers: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Client-Request-Id: test-123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-32k-v2","input":"..."}'` — include response headers.

ryan.cust: Will run that. Quick question — why 503s instead of 429s? I thought we'd get 429 when hitting limits.

maria.eng: Good question — 429s are explicit quota/rate-limit rejections. 503s in these cases come from the serving layer when instances are overloaded and choose to drop new work rather than accept and queue it (to preserve latency for in-flight requests). It's effectively graceful degradation when there are no safe slots to execute heavy token workloads.

jen.ops: Also note that long-context models (32k+) reduce per-instance concurrency because of KV cache and memory. So token footprint per-request is the dominant factor, not just RPM. You can hit token-TPM limits even if RPM looks modest.

alex.support: If you want us to dig in, we can correlate the req_ids with backend traces and confirm whether requests hit the same instance pool or were load-balanced to different nodes. If you prefer not to share req_ids publicly, DM them to me and maria.eng.

ryan.cust: Ok I'll DM two ids after repro. One last ask — any client-side knobs to avoid this short-term?

maria.eng: Short-term: cap concurrent gens to 3–5, add 200–500ms random jitter before retries, and prefer sequential embedding for the user save path. Medium-term: consider a burst-safe path — queue embeddings server-side and batch them every 200–500ms, or move embeds to a lower-cost model variant if quality allows.

ops-bot: Notice: we've flagged the 14:12 UTC window for rwd-32k-v2 for investigation. If additional logs are pasted, ops will attach traces. :mag:

ryan.cust: Thanks — testing now, will report back. Appreciate the quick help. :pray:
